title: Hello, request
objective: See that a web page arrives because your browser asks for it, and the server answers.

sources.title: MDN Web Docs: Overview of HTTP

simplifies: Real page loads also involve DNS lookups, connection setup, and usually many requests (one per image, script or stylesheet). This lesson shows a single request and response.

steps.caption: You type an address. Your browser sends a request to the server asking for the page.
The server answers with a response that contains the page. The browser then shows it.

quiz.prompt: In HTTP, who starts the exchange?

options.text: The browser, by sending a request
options.explanation: Right. HTTP is a client-server protocol: the client (usually the browser) sends the request, and the server responds.

options.text: The server, by sending the page when it is ready
options.explanation: Not in HTTP's basic model. The server waits for a request, then sends a response to it.

options.text: Both send at the same moment
options.explanation: No. There is a clear order: request first, then response.
